title: LEGO Pokémon Insiders reward 40911 Mini Pokémon Center back in stock
summary: The sought-after LEGO Pokémon Insiders Reward has returned for redemption, timed to coincide with a fresh wave of LEGO Pokémon sets landing this week.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to Brick Fanatics, the LEGO Insiders Reward 40911 Mini Pokémon Center is available to redeem again after first launching in late February and quickly selling out. The 223-piece build costs 2,500 Insiders points (roughly £15 in value) and measures 7cm tall, 10cm wide and 8cm deep.

Earning enough points typically requires around £315 ($380) of official LEGO purchases. Once redeemed via the Insiders Rewards Centre, the code must be used on a LEGO.com order within 60 days.

The reward's return coincides with a new wave of LEGO Pokémon sets, including 30729 Premier Ball, 30730 Trainer Supplies, and 72150 Munchlax, all reportedly releasing in August 2026. The wave also introduces SMART Play to the LEGO Pokémon theme, which LEGO was set to showcase via livestream.

Brick Fanatics notes the reward sold out quickly before, so it may not stick around for long this time either.

## Why it matters
Insiders Rewards like this one are a nice bonus for LEGO Pokémon collectors, but limited availability means fans hoping to grab one shouldn't hang about. It's also a sign of how actively LEGO is supporting the Pokémon theme with new sets and features.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on whether 40911 sells out again quickly, and watch for more details from LEGO's SMART Play livestream and the full August 2026 LEGO Pokémon set lineup.

bodyMarkdown:

The third project reimagines Disney's The Emperor's New Groove, built from 4,356 pieces with 10 proposed minifigures and several film-accurate scenes, including the famous "wrong lever" moment.

These additions bring the current second 2026 LEGO Ideas review to 59 submissions in total. It's worth remembering that reaching 10,000 supporters means a project enters review — it doesn't guarantee it will become an official set.

Separately, two already-confirmed LEGO Ideas sets, 21372 La Catrina and 21369 The X-Files, are reported to be launching officially very soon.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few routes for fan-designed concepts to become real sets, so seeing beloved franchises and quirky builds gain traction is exciting for the community. For collectors, it's also a signal of what themes and IPs might reach shelves next if LEGO gives the green light.

For LEGO Pokémon, the tech has been built around recreating Pokémon battles, giving it a clearer gameplay hook than the original LEGO Star Wars SMART Play sets. The sets confirmed so far include 30729 Premier Ball, 30730 Trainer Supplies, 72155 Berry Bash and 72156 Trainer's Buggy Adventure, with the range also introducing the theme's first-ever LEGO minifigure.

The LEGO Group has confirmed that anyone visiting a LEGO Store during the livestream will receive extra rewards, though exactly what those are hasn't been revealed yet.

This is the second wave of SMART Play sets after LEGO Star Wars, so it's an important test of whether the interactive brick concept can find a wider audience. title: Just a Third of Tonight's Retiring LEGO Sets Still in Stock in the UK
summary: Of 118 LEGO sets due to retire tonight, only 40 remain available to UK buyers, with several big names already sold out.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO retires sets twice a year, on 31 July and 31 December, to make room for new releases. Tonight's retirement wave affects 118 sets worldwide, but according to Brick Fanatics, only around 40 of these are still buyable in the UK before midnight.

Seven themes have already completely sold out in the UK ahead of the deadline: Marvel, Botanicals, Architecture, One Piece, Sonic the Hedgehog, The Legend of Zelda, and Batman/DC Super Heroes. Big-ticket sets like 75356 Executor Super Star Destroyer and 76417 Gringotts Wizarding Bank – Collectors' Edition have also gone.

Sets still available at the time of writing include LEGO Star Wars options such as 75347 TIE Bomber, 75404 Acclamator-Class Assault Ship and 75405 Home One Starcruiser, plus LEGO Ideas sets 21348 Dungeons & Dragons: Red Dragon's Tale and 21350 Jaws, and Harry Potter sets 76443 Hagrid & Harry's Motorcycle Ride and 76448 Fawkes Dumbledore's Phoenix.

From 1 August, 67 new sets are expected to take their place on shelves.

## Why it matters
Once a set retires, it typically won't be restocked by LEGO, and prices on the secondary market often rise afterwards. For collectors and builders hoping to grab a specific set at retail price, tonight is genuinely the last realistic chance in the UK before it's gone for good.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on official LEGO Shop stock levels for the remaining sets before midnight, and watch for the 67 new sets landing from 1 August as replacements roll out.

title: LEGO Fans Call For Built-In Lighting As X-Files And Sherlock Holmes Sets Highlight The Gap
summary: A new feature piece argues that sets like 21369 The X-Files and the retiring 10351 Sherlock Holmes Book Nook show why official built-in lighting is still missing from LEGO's lineup, with third-party brands currently filling the gap.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has published an opinion piece pointing out that two standout LEGO sets — 21369 The X-Files and the retiring 10351 Sherlock Holmes Book Nook — highlight a long-standing gap in LEGO's official range: built-in lighting.

Third-party companies such as Light My Bricks, Game of Bricks and Lightailing already sell retrofit lighting kits that add cables and LEDs to LEGO sets, and some rival construction brands include lighting straight out of the box. LEGO experimented with an in-house 'Night Mode' lighting concept back in 2020, but according to the piece, it didn't really catch on.

The article singles out book nook-style sets like Sherlock Holmes as a case in point — when closed, it's hard to appreciate the interior detail without some form of illumination, unlike display pieces such as modular buildings, which look great whether lit or not.

## Why it matters
Lighting is one of the most requested upgrades among AFOLs (Adult Fans of LEGO) and display builders, and it's a popular add-on for anyone building stadiums, book nooks or detailed interiors. For fans of compatible brick brands and custom accessories, this is a reminder that the third-party lighting market remains strong — and a potential opportunity for compatible brick makers to offer their own solutions.
